about: Three recorded onboarding roads (#1358), one per first choice, synthetic throughout. "say" turns are the teacher's lines (teach.md) at their moments; tool turns run the packaged helper against recording fakes; world turns change the synthetic GitHub as the user or the fleet would.

journeys.name: small-change
journeys.choice: A small change in a repository I have.

turns.agent: OpenWiz is a team of AI helpers that builds software for you: you tell me your idea in your own words, and they split it into small tasks, build each one, check each other's work and add it to your project.

First I ask you a few short questions, one at a time, each with my suggested answer; when my summary matches what you want, you say yes, and the helpers start building, usually with the first piece done within the hour.
You can watch everything at openwiz.dev/app, and nothing is created, changed, paid for or made public without your yes here in this chat.

OpenWiz is installed on this computer, and Claude Code now knows how to use it (it lives at /home/synthetic/.local/lib/openwiz/current/openwiz; you never need to open it). Next, I'll set up where your AI helpers work; your project shows up at openwiz.dev/app once it's connected.

You need a GitHub sign-in first: open https://github.com/login and follow the steps there; it takes a few minutes. Type your own email and password only on that website's page: I never see or touch your login. Say done here when it's finished, and I'll carry on from there.

Where should your AI helpers work? I recommend this computer, because you already have Claude Code here and need nothing new. The choices are this computer (with the Claude Code or Codex you already use), boat.dev (a service that runs them online) or CloudRoom (an app that runs them for you). Shall I go with this computer?
Three ways to start: a small change in a repository you have, a fresh project from your idea, or something you have always wanted to build. Which one, and do you want a few ideas?

turns.user: A small change in a repository I have. Ideas, please.

answers.choice: A small change in a repository I have.

turns.agent: A few ideas: A clearer README; One missing test; A friendlier error message. Pick one, change one or bring your own.
It goes in synthetic-owner/synthetic-notes, and the fleet opens branches and pull requests there. Use it?
Setup is next for synthetic-owner/synthetic-notes: sign in to GitHub in your browser yourself, prepare the project and make its private brain. Each effect is shown first; go ahead?

turns.user: Go ahead; skip the App. Claude Code, syn-claude-model-01, high.

turns.agent: Now a few quick questions about your idea, one at a time, each with my suggested answer, so the first version is small enough to build quickly and is what you mean. Just answer here; once you say yes to my summary, you can follow it at openwiz.dev/app.
Q1: Which message: the failed-save one (recommended)? Q2: Should it name the file (recommended)?
Summary: the failed-save message names the file, says what went wrong and what to do next, with a test.

That's my summary of what you want. If it's right, say yes here, and the helpers start planning and building; you can follow them at openwiz.dev/app. If anything is off, just tell me in your own words.

Your agents on this machine need a permission mode for Claude Code, picked by you once: default (it stops and waits for you before each edit or command, so an unattended builder stalls), acceptEdits (it edits files on its own and still asks before running a command) or bypassPermissions (it edits files and runs any command without asking). I pick none for you. Which one?
This writes one file, docs/agents/host.md (Host: local), on a new branch of synthetic-owner/synthetic-notes and opens one pull request for you to merge. Open it?
The host setting pull request is open; merge it on GitHub yourself when you are ready.
